title: Nonequilibrium steady states induced by stochastic mid-circuit measurements and resets on a quantum computer
authors: Jakob Murauer, Sabine Tornow, Gabriele Perfetto
abstract: Stochastic resetting has emerged as a versatile protocol to drive quantum many-body systems to non-equilibrium steady states by interspersing unitary dynamics with measurements and resets at random times. In spite of this, a quantum hardware validation of such non-equilibrium steady states is still missing. Here, we achieve this goal by first formulating a noisy discrete-time theory where unitary gates alternate with noisy mid-circuit projective measurements and conditional resets. This noisy conditional resetting theory is then demonstrated on a superconducting quantum processor for up to $N=7$ qubits. We consider, as a paradigmatic case, the unitary dynamics of the interacting Floquet transverse-field Ising model. The stationary state of the noisy conditional resetting agrees quantitatively with the experiments, and it shows crossover behavior related to the equilibrium quantum phase transition of the model. Our results might thus pave the way for the preparation of collective stationary states on noisy quantum devices and for further developments of quantum algorithms involving mid-circuit measurements.
summary: This paper develops and experimentally validates a theoretical framework for achieving Non-Equilibrium Steady States (NESS) in quantum many-body systems using stochastic mid-circuit measurements and resets. By applying this to the Floquet transverse-field Ising model on superconducting qubits, the authors show that engineered collective stationary states can be reliably prepared on noisy hardware. This work is significant because it provides a practical methodology for utilizing measurement feedback to control quantum dynamics away from thermal equilibrium.
main_problem: The core problem is validating theoretical predictions of Non-Equilibrium Steady States (NESS) induced by stochastic mid-circuit measurements and resets on actual quantum hardware.
main_result: The derived noisy conditional resetting theory quantitatively agrees with experimental data on superconducting qubits, demonstrating that collective stationary states can be engineered despite noise.
method: The authors combine theoretical derivations using discrete Laplace transforms for NESS calculation with extensive experimental implementation on a superconducting processor.
model_or_system: The system is the interacting Floquet transverse-field Ising model simulated on a superconducting quantum processor (ibm_marrakesh). The dynamics involve alternating unitary evolution ($U_	heta$) with stochastic measurements and conditional resets.
key_observables: Longitudinal magnetization density ($\langle m angle$) and squared magnetization density ($\langle m^2 angle$).
important_parameters: Transverse field strength ($h$), coupling strengths ($J$), system size ($N=3, 5, 7$ qubits).
main_assumptions: The theory models resets as a semi-Markov process and accounts for readout errors; the experimental analysis compares various noise models (e.g., depolarizing channel vs. noisy reset state model).
figures_summary: Figures compare measured magnetization versus theoretical predictions across different qubit numbers, showing crossover behavior related to quantum phase transitions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from general theory derivations of NESS in discrete time (using Laplace transforms) to applying this framework to the specific Floquet TFIM model, culminating in hardware implementation and noise characterization.
why_interesting: This work bridges fundamental non-equilibrium statistical mechanics concepts with cutting-edge quantum hardware capabilities, providing a concrete pathway for engineering complex steady states beyond thermal equilibrium.
